svg.title: Floating-point fields and little-endian byte order
svg.desc: The first panel compares the logical sign, exponent, and stored fraction fields of binary16, bfloat16, binary32, and binary64. The second panel shows the same fields grouped into bytes in increasing memory address order on a little-endian system. Byte order changes, but bits within each byte are shown from bit seven to bit zero.
svg.metadata: Generated deterministically by scripts/generate_floating_point_layout_figure.py. Field widths follow IEEE 754 binary16, binary32, and binary64, and the common bfloat16 layout.
svg.text: Floating-point fields and little-endian byte order
Field widths determine precision and range; byte order determines storage in memory
most-significant bit at left; least-significant bit at right
B Bytes in memory on a little-endian system
lower address at left; higher address at right
Within each byte, the diagram uses the conventional bit 7 → bit 0 display.
For normal values, p = stored fraction bits + 1
The extra leading significand bit is implicit, not stored.
Little endian reverses byte significance in memory; it does not reverse all bits.
